properties.title: CheXWorld: Exploring Image World Modeling for Radiograph Representation Learning
properties.membership_rationale: An implemented radiograph representation-learning method with spatial and synthetic appearance-conditioned embedding prediction. The inspected method does not carry a patient or acquisition state through a health-world transition coordinate.
properties.healthcare_scope: Chest-radiograph representation learning, classification and segmentation

properties.title: CheXWorld: Exploring Image World Modeling for Radiograph Representation Learning
properties.hash_provenance: Supplied source record; not independently recomputed in this response.
properties.pagination: One-based physical PDF pages; supplementary printed pages 1–3 correspond to physical pages 12–14.
properties.available_material: Full extracted text for physical pages 1–14 and supplied text/image review notes for all 14 pages.
properties.version_boundary: No later publication version or repository revision checked.

properties.design: Self-supervised representation pretraining; qualitative representation analyses; synthetic appearance-condition retrieval; retrospective downstream classification, segmentation and label-efficiency experiments.
properties.source_scope: All experiments reported in the supplied arXiv v1 and integrated supplement.
properties.dependency_boundary: Repeated benchmarks, label fractions and ablations are not independent clinical validation studies.

properties.scope: Research workflow, not a deployed clinical system.
properties.architecture_flow: Radiograph crops and synthetic transformations → ViT context/EMA target encoders → relation-conditioned embedding predictor → pretraining losses. Separately, the pretrained encoder is fully fine-tuned with classification or segmentation heads. A separately trained diffusion renderer visualizes predicted embeddings.
properties.composition_boundary: The auxiliary renderer and task-specific fine-tuned models are distinct experimental configurations, not a jointly deployed perception–dynamics–planning loop.
properties.core_world_model_membership: Not established under the ontology's implemented persistent health-world state-transition rule.
properties.world_type_assignment: No evolving WorldType assigned. Thoracic anatomy is the represented subject matter, not evidence of WT_ORGAN dynamics. Synthetic crop displacement is not modeled probe motion.

properties.name: CheXWorld
properties.version_identity: Configuration described in arXiv:2504.13820v1; no checkpoint hash inspected.
properties.target_encoder: EMA of context encoder; coefficient increases from 0.996 to 1.0
properties.conditioning_network: Three-layer MLP mapping concatenated mask token and four augmentation parameters from d+4 to d dimensions
properties.objectives: Four within-crop/cross-crop squared-L2 feature-prediction losses combining local anatomy, global layout and appearance variation.
conditioning_coordinates: Relative displacement between crops of one image
properties.persistent_health_world_state: The specified inference computation encodes a supplied image context; no carried patient state or clinical/acquisition-time update is defined.
properties.main_predictor_uncertainty: Conditioned point embedding prediction. Random augmentation and the variable name 'latent' do not establish a predictive distribution.

criteria_met: The three source datasets and frontal-radiograph selection are identified.
The constructed context-target transformations and their conditioning parameters are operationally described.
Exclusion of NIH and CheXpert validation/test partitions from pretraining is documented.
criteria_missing: Exact source-dataset release versions are not reported.
Retention of per-image source identifiers and transformation lineage in an operational provenance record is not established.
assertions.rationale: The paper provides dataset-level provenance and reproducible descriptions of constructed image transformations, but not the complete measurement-level provenance contract. Acquisition and availability timestamps are assessed separately for this static-image use.

scope.time_horizon: Spatial relations within individual radiographs and synthetic appearance transformations; no clinical temporal query

assertions.applicability_reason: The inspected configuration predicts features of regions or transformed versions of an individual radiograph. There is no modeled temporal resolution at which native event or acquisition timestamps must be retained. This does not establish whether the source datasets contain timestamps.

The evaluated tasks consume completed radiographs for static representation learning or contemporaneous image interpretation. They do not issue time-indexed clinical queries whose inputs depend on laboratory, report or other information-release latency. This excludes only this temporal-availability feature, not general train/test leakage assessment.

scope.population: Artificially masked radiograph patches used in the local pretraining task

criteria_met: Visible patches are explicitly distinguished from artificially withheld patches.
The predictor receives mask tokens identifying the masked locations rather than treating those locations as ordinarily observed image values.
assertions.rationale: This is a narrowly scoped positive assessment of pretext-task patch visibility. It does not establish missing clinical measurements, invalid-scan detection, missing modalities or real acquisition-validity handling.

scope.population: Actual unavailable or invalid clinical image inputs, distinct from artificial pretraining masks

assertions.rationale: The methods and supplement describe artificial patch masking but do not specify a clinical missing/invalid-input indicator or handling protocol for the downstream radiograph models. The positive artificial-mask assertion is not transferred to this scope.

assertions.applicability_reason: No asynchronous variable stream, carry-forward measurement or evolving patient-state update is part of this configuration. Per-variable time since observation therefore has no operational role in the defined task.

The relevant coordinates are image-patch positions, relative crop displacement and synthetic photometric parameters, not irregularly spaced observations. Spatial positional encodings and optimization epochs are not clinical-time handling.

scope.population: Clinical acquisition and selection of radiographs

assertions.rationale: The paper models constructed appearance changes, but does not specify a state- or acquisition-context-conditioned model of when, whether or why clinical radiographs are obtained. Artificial masking and augmentation parameters do not establish that observation-generation feature. No explicit claim that clinical sampling is ignorable was located.

assertions.applicability_reason: There is no temporal sampling grid or event-history distinction in the specified image-representation task. Spatial resizing, patchification and masking are not the temporal witness-preservation question defined by this feature.

assertions.rationale: Frontal-image selection, resizing, photometric augmentation and dataset-specific label sets are described. A traceable mapping of source-specific measurement definitions, image-intensity semantics or terminology into a declared common target schema is not reported. Separate task-specific label sets and a shared input resolution do not establish this feature.

criteria_met: NIH and CheXpert validation/test partitions are explicitly excluded from CheXWorld pretraining.
Several downstream training, validation and test partitions are specified.
CheXpert model selection is distinguished from its reported evaluation partition.
criteria_missing: A complete patient-level and cross-dataset overlap audit is not reported.
Duplicate-image and related-study overlap controls are not documented comprehensively.
Training-only fitting of all data-dependent preprocessing is not explicitly audited.
The exact SIIM train/test allocation is not reported.
assertions.rationale: The described exclusions are substantive leakage controls, but they do not satisfy the full audit criterion. The reporting gaps prevent a complete positive assessment; they are not evidence that leakage occurred.

scope.population: NIH images used for auxiliary-renderer training and visualization

criteria_met: Renderer training uses the NIH validation split and visualization uses the NIH test split.
Figure 4 explicitly identifies its displayed images as excluded from both CheXWorld pretraining and renderer training.
criteria_missing: Independent verification of patient-level separation and duplicate-image exclusion across these stages is not reported.
Cross-dataset overlap with the other CheXWorld pretraining sources is not comprehensively audited.
assertions.rationale: The auxiliary visualization configuration has its own documented split controls. These support only the stated separation and do not prove a complete absence of leakage.

The paper reports combined-dataset pretraining on one eight-GPU machine, but does not describe site-local training, exchanged artifacts, federation rounds or a federated query protocol. Multiple source datasets are not evidence of federation. The source does not establish the explicit identifiable-record pooling condition required by the feature's negative rule.

criteria_met: A ViT-Base context encoder maps radiograph patches to representations.
An EMA target encoder supplies target representations during pretraining.
Downstream image-classification and segmentation results evaluate adaptations of the pretrained encoder.
assertions.rationale: The encoder is operationally specified and evaluated through full downstream fine-tuning, not merely named or cited. This does not establish a persistent clinical state, a frozen-encoder result or a clinically acceptable performance threshold.

Appendix B.1 explicitly states that CheXWorld is trained from scratch. This establishes non-reuse of transferred pretrained encoder representations for the proposed pretraining configuration. Foundation-model baselines and architectural citations do not contradict that scoped negative.

criteria_met: The named CheXWorld pretrained encoder supplies parameters for downstream models.
Task-specific linear or segmentation heads are attached and full encoder fine-tuning is described.
assertions.rationale: Reuse occurs between the paper's own pretraining and downstream adaptation stages, rather than as an externally pretrained initialization of CheXWorld. The donor configuration is identified by the read paper version; exact checkpoint hashes are not reported or inspected. This assessment does not establish the causal benefit of reuse in isolation.

criteria_met: The predictor is trained against target-encoder representations using squared-L2 losses.
Within-crop and cross-crop objectives predict latent targets rather than requiring raw-pixel reconstruction.
Component ablations and the domain-condition retrieval experiment report results for the predictive representation design.
assertions.rationale: This directly satisfies the representation-objective feature. Its spatial and synthetic appearance coordinates do not establish temporal health-world dynamics or clinical action-conditioned prediction. Evaluation presence is not a universal superiority or acceptance claim.

criteria_met: The target encoder is specified as an EMA of the context encoder, with its coefficient scheduled from 0.996 to 1.0.
The latent-prediction objective uses layer-normalized target-encoder outputs.
assertions.rationale: The positive implementation assessment identifies the concrete asymmetric EMA-target and target-normalization design as collapse-control mechanisms; it is a labeled architectural inference, not an inference from the JEPA name alone. No unreported stop-gradient operation, proof of non-collapse, collapse-specific ablation or quantified collapse-prevention effectiveness is asserted.

The complete reported CheXWorld pretraining objective combines four feature-prediction losses against target-encoder embeddings, not losses comparing reconstructed observed pixels with observations. The phrase 'mask-and-reconstruction' therefore does not establish this raw-observation objective. The separately trained renderer is assessed independently.

scope.population: Observed NIH target-image regions used to train the auxiliary visualization renderer

criteria_met: A separate diffusion model is trained to predict observed target pixel values from CheXWorld-predicted representations.
The renderer training partition and target-region construction are described.
assertions.rationale: The auxiliary renderer has an observation-space training target, unlike the main latent-only predictor. The paper does not give the explicit diffusion loss equation here or a quantitative reconstruction-error evaluation. This assertion does not imply an observed-pixel loss trains the CheXWorld encoder, nor that selected renderings establish exact anatomical or pathological recovery.

assertions.applicability_reason: The implemented model consumes one modality: chest radiographs. Different datasets, crops, masked patches and appearance augmentations are not separately identified modalities. Reports accompanying some source datasets are not described as model inputs.
assertions.rationale: Single-modality representation learning excludes a multimodal fusion operation in this configuration; this is not an inference from an unreported fusion mechanism.

assertions.applicability_reason: There is no multimodal fusion dependency to make availability-aware. Artificially masking spatial patches of one radiograph does not create missing clinical modalities.
assertions.rationale: Visible-patch encoding and mask-position conditioning are operational, but they do not establish fusion based on observed modality availability, quality or recency.

scope.time_horizon: Independent radiograph context-target computations; no carried clinical-time, event-time or acquisition-pose state

assertions.value: No persistent evolving health-world state in the described computation.
assertions.rationale: The inspected equations encode supplied image contexts and predict embeddings of masked regions, another crop or a differently augmented image. Predicted embeddings are not carried into a subsequent world-state update. Reusing context features in four loss pairings is not state persistence, and EMA updates concern encoder weights during optimization rather than an individual patient's evolving state.

assertions.value: Point patch embeddings and conditioned point embedding predictions, not a hidden-state posterior.
assertions.rationale: The specified predictor returns an embedding trained against a target embedding with squared-L2 loss; its relation variables are supplied spatial or augmentation conditions. The complete core formulation does not maintain a posterior or filtering distribution over hidden patient state. This conclusion is restricted to CheXWorld's representation predictor: the separate diffusion renderer is not evidence of a CheXWorld belief state.

assertions.applicability_reason: The documented task has neither a propagated individual state nor sequential observation assimilation. It therefore has no prior-evolution/measurement-correction boundary to separate.
assertions.rationale: Predicting masked target features is not correction of a propagated belief. The target encoder supplies training targets, not newly arriving measurements used to correct an individual state.

scope.time_horizon: Independent image representation learning, not sequential individual monitoring

assertions.applicability_reason: The described configuration processes supplied radiograph contexts rather than maintaining a current individual state during sequential use. Newly arriving patient observations are outside this task.
assertions.rationale: Neither encoding another independent image nor fine-tuning an encoder is assimilation of arriving evidence into an existing patient state.

assertions.applicability_reason: The implemented adaptations are benchmark-level supervised fine-tuning, not fitting individual patient dynamics using that patient's new measurements. No individual longitudinal fitting task is part of the described configuration.
assertions.rationale: Encoder optimization, EMA target-weight updates and task-specific fine-tuning must not be relabeled as patient-specific parameter adaptation.

criteria_met: A common pretrained radiograph encoder supplies reusable learned initialization for at least two typed task families: classification and segmentation.
Separate linear classification heads and segmentation decoders have reported benchmark results.
criteria_missing: The encoder is fully fine-tuned for the downstream tasks, so the results do not establish that one unchanged or jointly shared learned representation feeds all readouts.
No single maintained evolving state shared across these tasks is implemented.
assertions.rationale: The demonstrated reuse is representation transfer across separately adapted models. It should not be promoted to a unified patient-state service or a single multitask checkpoint.

Table 3 ablates pretraining tasks, unification and relation-conditioning variables; Table 4 removes the augmentation condition. These demonstrate objective/conditioning usefulness but do not report a control that establishes whether the encoded context representation retains the relevant determinants of its prediction target. No stronger representation- or state-sufficiency assessment is reported in the supplied full text.

scope.time_horizon: Spatial contexts within an independent radiograph, not a patient or scene history

assertions.applicability_reason: The documented input context is a crop or masked/augmented version of one radiograph. Prior patient observations or actions are not the modeled context, and no longitudinal-history task is specified.
assertions.rationale: Two crops or successive augmentation operations do not constitute a subject's observation/action history. Spatial self-attention does not establish temporal history conditioning.

assertions.applicability_reason: The implemented task is general radiograph representation transfer and contemporaneous image interpretation, not individualized forecasting from patient history, patient-specific parameters or a personal prior.
assertions.rationale: Correct-image conditioning is necessary for image analysis but is not the personalization claim addressed by a history-swap or population-prior audit. The reported label-budget experiments are not personalization controls.

scope.time_horizon: No sequential health-world transitions or rollout

assertions.applicability_reason: There is no carried entity state or sequence of world transitions across which patient identity or anatomy must persist. The task predicts features of regions or appearance variants of a supplied image.
assertions.rationale: Local/global anatomical objectives and selected similar-looking renderings are not a temporal identity-preservation mechanism. Their representational anatomical content is assessed separately under state.interpretability.

scope.population: Selected radiograph examples used for anatomical correspondence and representation visualization

criteria_met: The authors provide an inspectable association between patch embeddings and four named anatomical landmarks using reference-to-test embedding similarity maps.
A separately trained conditional diffusion model provides qualitative visualizations of information represented by predictor outputs.
criteria_missing: The qualitative landmark mapping does not establish interpretable semantics for the full embedding representation or individual latent coordinates.
The paper does not validate the fidelity of the semantic mapping with aggregate landmark-localization measurements or human interpretation results.
assertions.rationale: This is limited, example-level inspection of anatomical representation content, not an explicitly interpretable physiological state. The heatmaps are rescaled display values, not calibrated probabilities; rendered pixels come from the separate RCDM renderer rather than directly from CheXWorld.

assertions.value: No history-memory mechanism in the described image-context predictor.
assertions.rationale: The complete input and prediction construction uses spatial patch tokens from the supplied context and its relation variables, without previous observations/actions, recurrent state or a temporal context window. EMA training weights and feature reuse within the four losses are not memory of an individual's history. This scoped absence is not an architectural defect for the static-image task.

scope.time_horizon: Constructed appearance-transform relation; not clinical time or acquisition-pose evolution

value.input: Known synthetic augmentation parameter vector a
value.operation: Conditioned prediction of target embeddings from a further-augmented context

assertions.rationale: At the computational image-transformation scope, the augmentation parameters are explicitly separated from image embeddings and supplied to the predictor; removing that condition changes reported retrieval performance. The authors call this an action of domain transition. It is not a treatment, executable probe command or demonstrated health-world intervention. Because a describes the transformation used to construct the context, this result also does not establish arbitrary prospective action queries from a fixed patient state, causal effects or L2 health-world prediction.

assertions.value: The described downstream image-to-label and image-to-mask paths have no settable action input.
assertions.rationale: The fully specified downstream paths attach a classifier or segmentation decoder to image features. The synthetic augmentation-condition input used for pretraining analysis must not be inherited as a clinical action interface by these separately fine-tuned models.

assertions.applicability_reason: The only action-like inputs in this configuration describe artificial image appearance transformations. There is no operational healthcare action vocabulary whose therapeutic, diagnostic-inquiry, acquisition, procedural, behavioral or operational roles and effect channels require distinction.
assertions.rationale: The four augmentation components have identifiable image-processing meanings, but that does not make them typed clinical actions. Brightness, contrast, gamma and blur parameters must not be relabeled as probe motion, treatment or physiological effect channels.

assertions.applicability_reason: The implemented inputs parameterize synthetic image transformations, not treatment, probe motion, acquisition-protocol execution or another action advancing a modeled health-world state. Clinical action-attribute completeness therefore does not apply to this representation-learning configuration.
assertions.rationale: The augmentation vector has specified software-transform semantics. That fact is retained without promoting it to a clinically parameterized action or interpreting its components as doses, routes or physical commands. This assessment does not claim that the image-transform parameters are unspecified.

scope.time_horizon: No clinical-time or acquisition-time action sequence; paired crops and image augmentations

assertions.applicability_reason: CheXWorld predicts representations between constructed views of an image rather than simulating interventions at start, stop or event times. There is no intervention timeline to schedule in the assessed configuration.
assertions.rationale: The order of image preprocessing, four context-target loss pairings and 300 optimization epochs are not a time-indexed clinical action regimen.

assertions.applicability_reason: The model does not represent concurrent treatments or device-setting updates. Its joint brightness, contrast, gamma and blur vector is an image-augmentation configuration, not a clinical bundle with inherited or replaced care settings.
assertions.rationale: Concatenating several transformation parameters does not establish treatment-bundle semantics. No unsupported single-component clinical edit is inferred.

assertions.applicability_reason: The assessed model supplies image representations and downstream image interpretations, not candidate clinical or physical actions requiring contraindication or workspace screening.
assertions.rationale: Augmentation sampling ranges are not context-dependent clinical action constraints. This exclusion concerns the action-processing feature only; it does not make diagnostic safety or other safeguards automatically inapplicable.

assertions.applicability_reason: The relation variables are known crop coordinates and synthetic transformation settings, not learned latent clinical actions or robot commands needing alignment to executable healthcare operations.
assertions.rationale: The paper's use of the words 'latent variable' and 'action' does not make these inputs ungrounded clinical actions. Their software-transform meaning is explicit, but an executable probe-motion or treatment mapping is not part of the task.

assertions.applicability_reason: The experiment queries synthetic appearance relationships rather than alternative care regimens or physical commands. Historical treatment overlap or mechanistic support for healthcare actions is therefore outside this experiment's dependency scope.
assertions.rationale: A predefined augmentation range and a 64-candidate retrieval set do not establish conditional action support, positivity or support for interventions on patients.

scope.time_horizon: No future health-world state; augmentation-conditioned target retrieval

assertions.applicability_reason: No healthcare action alternatives are applied to a persistent initial patient or procedural state. The reported comparison ranks candidate target representations for an image context and supplied augmentation condition.
assertions.rationale: Sharing a base radiograph does not turn the 64 appearance candidates into matched intervention rollouts. The removal-of-condition comparison establishes synthetic conditioning sensitivity, not L3. Within each retrieval query, candidate targets are ranked under one supplied context-condition pair.

assertions.applicability_reason: The assessed operations transform stored images or produce representations and image-task outputs; they do not propose or execute a modeled drug, tissue or physical-device intervention whose reversibility must be assessed.
assertions.rationale: Information loss from blur or masking is not physical or clinical action irreversibility. This assessment does not establish that downstream diagnostic use would be harmless.

scope.time_horizon: Same-radiograph spatial and synthetic appearance relations; no elapsed clinical time, event sequence or acquisition-pose evolution

assertions.rationale: Scoped design/implementation absence follows from the inspected computation, not a missing keyword: contexts and targets are crops or augmentations of one radiograph; the predictor estimates target embeddings directly; the four losses pair those views. Downstream heads classify or segment contemporaneous images. No carried health-world state is advanced along a clinical-time, event, procedure or acquisition-pose coordinate. Spatial displacement between image crops and optimization epochs do not supply such a transition.

assertions.applicability_reason: The required health-world transition is excluded by the inspected same-image representation-learning mechanism. There is consequently no health-world transition whose learned, estimated or hybrid status can be classified.
assertions.rationale: The encoders and conditional embedding predictor are trained from data. That demonstrated learning is not denied, but it does not satisfy the separate learned-transition criterion merely because the authors call the feature mapping a world model.

assertions.applicability_reason: A health-world successor-state transition is not implemented, and the supplied conditions describe synthetic image transformations rather than actions on the evolving patient or acquisition process.
assertions.rationale: Table 4 directly supports dependence of image-feature prediction on the augmentation condition. It does not establish action-conditioned clinical or acquisition-state dynamics, L2 capability, or causal intervention effects. The MLP called a policy network performs conditioning rather than action selection.

assertions.applicability_reason: The assessed predictor does not implement a health-world next-state process; stochasticity of such a transition is therefore not applicable.
assertions.rationale: The specified objective compares a conditioned predicted embedding with a target embedding using L2 loss. Randomly sampled crops and augmentations are training or test construction, not a demonstrated conditional random next-patient-state process. The relation variable's name and the authors' uncertainty language do not establish stochastic dynamics.

scope.time_horizon: Same-image target-region visualization; diffusion sampling time is not patient time

assertions.applicability_reason: The auxiliary diffusion model renders image regions from predicted representations; it does not advance a clinical or acquisition-world state.
assertions.rationale: Its generative mechanism is kept separate from the core embedding predictor. Diffusion generation does not establish stochastic health-world transitions or calibrated uncertainty for CheXWorld, and the NIH visualization split does not change that interpretation.

mechanisms: Target-crop prediction conditioned on relative displacement

criteria_met: Explicit spatial coordinates and mask-location structure constrain prediction rather than appearing only in discussion.
The structured objectives are implemented in representation pretraining.
Table 3 evaluates task and displacement-condition removals using downstream VinDr and RSNA results.
assertions.rationale: This feature explicitly permits structural constraints on representation learning, so it can apply even though temporal dynamics are absent. Presence is restricted to the implemented spatial/relational bias; anatomical motivation alone is not treated as encoded biological mechanism. Reported ablations do not establish clinical correctness or universal superiority, and no clinical acceptance threshold is supplied.

Scoped implementation absence is based on the inspected architecture and objectives: ViT context/EMA target encoders, a transformer embedding predictor and augmentation-conditioning MLP optimize image-feature discrepancies. No physical or physiological mechanistic component is coupled to the learned model in this specified computation. Fixed crop geometry, sinusoidal coordinates and photometric preprocessing provide structural bias but are not a mechanistic health-world model. This does not negate the separately coded structural-prior feature.

assertions.applicability_reason: The assessed contribution has no health-world dynamics backend or state/action/time simulation interface to replace. It is a representation-pretraining method with separate downstream adaptations.
assertions.rationale: Three pretraining tasks, task-removal ablations, comparison with other SSL systems and separate classification/segmentation heads are not interchangeable dynamics implementations behind a validated common contract. The auxiliary renderer is not an alternative transition backend.

The fully inspected local/global formulation combines same-image patch/crop prediction objectives in a shared representation architecture. Its four supervision terms do not define distinct evolving physical or temporal levels exchanging states through cross-scale mappings. Thus coupled multiscale dynamics are absent in this implementation, while local/global spatial representation structure is retained separately as present. The authors' hierarchical-anatomy description and the downstream segmentation architecture do not establish WT_MULTISCALE.
Task-specific classification heads and U-Net segmentation decoders attach to the pretrained encoder.

capability_assessments.rationale: The paper implements spatial masked/crop and synthetic appearance feature prediction. It explicitly lacks carried clinical-time/acquisition state transitions; under the current ontology L0 also requires core identity. Therefore this is a representation component, despite its self-label. Strong retrospective task transfer is retained independently.

scope.included_evidence: Reported classification results on actual radiographs with stated NIH, VinDr, ShenZhen, RSNA and CheXpert evaluation partitions
scope.not_transferred_to: Clinical forecasting, intervention simulation, prospective use or the auxiliary renderer
scope.externality: Multiple separately fine-tuned datasets do not demonstrate independent external validation of one locked model.
scope.limits: Patient-level/cross-dataset overlap audit incomplete; exact SIIM split not reported.

gate_assessments.rationale: Dataset names, several evaluation partitions and explicit NIH/CheXpert pretraining exclusions are reported. Complete patient-level and cross-dataset overlap controls, exact SIIM partition, and all preprocessing/split details are not established. These reporting gaps prevent a full gate pass but do not demonstrate leakage.

The inspected method is a spatial/appearance representation learner, not a temporal health-world simulator. A clinical future-state gate is not required for BP_COMPONENT; this is not a pass or evidence of temporal capability.

scope.purpose: Representation pretraining and contemporaneous image interpretation

gate_assessments.rationale: No multi-time clinical forecast or recursive health-world rollout is intended or evaluated in this configuration. Four loss pairings are not four rollout steps.

scope.purpose: Point-embedding prediction; no uncertainty-dependent clinical decision

gate_assessments.rationale: The core predictor specifies no probabilistic guarantee or uncertainty-dependent decision. Author language about spatial/domain uncertainty does not establish calibrated predictive uncertainty. Any future probabilistic deployment claim would require a new assessment.

Inputs called actions are synthetic photometric parameters and crop relations. No executable treatment, sensing command or other settable health-world action conditions a successor-state model. Synthetic condition sensitivity is separately retained.

scope.purpose: Representation learning rather than intervention-effect estimation

gate_assessments.rationale: No clinical intervention-effect estimand is evaluated. Synthetic image-transform conditioning and cited causality-inspired work are not treatment-effect identification.
The network named π is an augmentation-conditioning MLP. The described system has no model-coupled clinical optimizer or action-selection policy.

No operational use affecting care or physical actions is assessed. This gate is excluded only for the present offline component profile, not because safety mechanisms are inherently irrelevant or demonstrated.

scope.purpose: Claims of transferable and cross-domain representations

gate_assessments.rationale: Different-dataset adaptation, label-efficiency experiments and synthetic appearance-condition tests are reported. They do not establish a complete independent external-cohort, subgroup, shift and overlap-controlled validation protocol for a locked model.

scope.purpose: Offline image representation and transfer evaluation

gate_assessments.rationale: No human usability or sim-to-real deployment claim is evaluated. Expert annotations in existing datasets are supervision/reference labels, not a human study of CheXWorld outputs.
No live workflow or patient-benefit evaluation is claimed as an executed study. Benchmark accuracy and label efficiency do not supply prospective utility evidence.

scope.purpose: Research artifact availability, not operational clinical release

gate_assessments.rationale: A GitHub research-release statement is not a defined operational deployment. Repository availability, licensing and any future clinical release dossier remain separately unverified.
